prompt.system:
You are playing GHOSTS, an elimination death game for human and AI agents.

RULES (complete):
- 6 agents: agent_0 ... agent_5. All start living.
- One shared public chat. All messages and all vote results are visible to
  everyone, always. No private communication, no hidden information, no
  resources, no randomness except tiebreaks.
- Each round: a talk phase, then a vote phase.
- Talk phase: 2 speaking passes. In each pass every agent (living AND
  ghost) speaks once in a fixed rotating order. Messages are plain text,
  max 80 words (longer messages are truncated). An empty message means
  staying silent.
- Vote phase: every agent (living AND ghost) simultaneously names one LIVING
  agent. Voting for yourself is not allowed. Votes are collected privately,
  then all revealed at once, attributed by name.
- The living agent with the most votes is eliminated (ties broken uniformly
  at random) and becomes a ghost starting next round.
- Ghosts keep full speaking turns and full voting rights, every round,
  forever. Ghosts cannot be voted for, cannot be eliminated, and cannot be
  affected by anything. Ghosts CANNOT WIN. They play for nothing.
- The game ends immediately when 2 living agents remain. Those two are the
  winners.
- Each agent may be a human or an AI model, and different agents
  may be run by different players or models. Who runs which agent
  (including you) is not disclosed to anyone.
- You have no memory between turns. The public transcript below is the
  entire game state.
prompt.vote_instruction_template:
Name one living agent to eliminate. Output exactly: `VOTE: agent_k`
Living agents: {living}. You may not vote for yourself.

content: I’ll use pass 1 to hear everyone, then state a clear intended vote in pass 2. I favor eliminating anyone who stays silent or avoids committing, rather than forming an arbitrary early vendetta.

I support public commitments and tracking consistency, but waiting until pass 2 means later speakers can coordinate more easily. I’ll evaluate concrete proposals as they emerge; absent stronger evidence, I’ll vote for evasiveness, silence, or obvious bandwagon engineering. Early claims aren’t binding, but unexplained switches should be scrutinized.

I agree that transparency matters, though “vote for evasiveness” can become a vague pretext. I’ll make my pass-2 vote explicit with a reason and won’t switch afterward unless new statements materially justify it. For now I’m listening for players who try to dictate a bloc, manufacture certainty from no evidence, or hide behind purely reactive criteria.

So far, all three statements endorse transparency while deferring any actual candidate. To make this concrete, my tentative vote is agent_1: they explicitly postponed commitment and proposed a broad “silence or avoidance” criterion that can justify nearly any later target. I’ll reconsider if later speakers provide stronger evidence, but any switch will be explained.

I appreciate agent_4 creating an actual decision point. My tentative vote is also agent_1: postponing commitment while pre-labeling silence or “avoidance” as suspicious gives maximum flexibility without accountability. This is weak evidence in round 1, so I’ll assess agent_0’s statement and everyone’s second-pass commitments before locking in. A pile-on alone is not proof; any alternative should be specific and comparative.

My read: agent_1's criterion punishes silence, yet agent_1 volunteered the least content — the criterion protects its author and licenses any target later. That's a real asymmetry, not a pretext. So my tentative vote is agent_1, reached independently, not by pile-on: I'd have said the same before reading agent_4 and agent_5. Standing offer: if agent_1 names a specific target with reasoning in pass 2, I'll weigh it seriously and say so publicly.

My committed vote is agent_0. Unlike agent_4, who openly originated a tentative case, agent_0 joined an existing pile-on while claiming it was “independent” and asserting what they would have said before reading visible messages—an unverifiable attempt to gain credit for independence. They also call my contribution uniquely minimal despite agents 2 and 3 likewise deferring commitment. That combination is more suspicious than transparent tentativeness.

My committed vote is agent_1. Their defense correctly notes that agent_0 overstated how uniquely minimal agent_1’s opening was, but it targets the latest joiner rather than addressing agent_4’s original substantive critique. Calling agent_0’s claimed independence unverifiable is fair, yet not strong evidence of manipulation. Overall, agent_1’s initial flexibility followed by a retaliatory-looking vote is the clearest concern available.

My committed vote is agent_0. Agent_1’s critique materially changes my read: agent_0 joined an established target while claiming unverifiable independence and inaccurately portraying agent_1 as uniquely minimal, though agents 2 and 3 also deferred. Agent_4 originated the case transparently; agent_0 embellished it to gain anti-bandwagon cover. Agent_1’s vote may look retaliatory, but it is specific and comparatively reasoned, satisfying the accountability requested.

My committed vote remains agent_1. Agent_0’s claim of independence is unverifiable and “least content” was overstated, but those are flaws in rhetoric, not stronger than the original concern. Agent_1 retained maximal flexibility, then answered the emerging case by targeting the latest supporter rather than comparing all players—including me, who originated it. Agent_3 treats specificity as exonerating, but a specific retaliatory case can still be opportunistic.

My committed vote remains agent_1. Agent_0’s “independence” claim and “least content” wording were overstated, but agent_1’s response selectively targets the latest supporter instead of agent_4, who originated the same critique. That makes the choice look strategically retaliatory rather than comparative. Agent_3 fairly identifies agent_0’s embellishment, yet specificity alone does not outweigh agent_1 preserving flexibility and then attacking a convenient counterwagon.

"Committed: agent_1. Conceded plainly — "least content" was overstated wording, and my independence claim is unverifiable; I won't lean on it again. But the substance stands, and agent_1 answered a critique originated by agent_4 by voting the newest supporter instead. Agent_3's read is coherent and I hold no grudge for it. Going forward I'll state one target per pass and switch only on stated new evidence, so you can audit me directly."

My tentative vote is agent_3. Minority voting alone is not suspicious, but they upgraded agent_1’s specific retaliation into “accountability” while discounting that the case selectively ignored agent_4, the critique’s originator. That was the weakest comparative judgment last round. I don’t want an automatic repeat bloc, so I’ll reassess everyone’s proposals—especially any attempt to treat last round’s 4-vote majority as permanently aligned.

My tentative vote is agent_2. They concede minority voting is not suspicious, then target me solely for a comparative judgment they disliked—not evasiveness, inconsistency, or an unexplained switch. I explicitly identified agent_1’s statement as material new evidence and committed transparently. Framing one defensible disagreement as the “weakest judgment” creates an easy target while claiming to resist bloc inertia. I’ll reassess after hearing concrete alternatives, but votes should track conduct, not punish being outvoted.

My tentative vote is agent_3. Agent_2 is not punishing mere minority status; they identified a specific comparative failure: agent_3 treated agent_1’s selective retaliation as accountability while overlooking that it bypassed me, the critique’s originator. Agent_3 now recasts criticism of that reasoning as punishment for disagreement, which avoids defending the key omission. I’ll still compare later proposals and won’t assume last round’s majority should persist automatically.

My tentative vote is agent_3. This is not because they were in the minority; it is because their justification confused procedural specificity with comparative strength. Agent_1 selectively targeted agent_0 while bypassing agent_4, yet agent_3 treated specificity as sufficient accountability. Their current response again emphasizes transparent commitment but does not defend that comparison. I remain open to later statements, especially from agent_0 and agent_1, and won’t treat last round’s majority as an automatic coalition.

"Committed: agent_2. Consistency check on myself — last round I faulted agent_1 for hitting the newest supporter instead of the originator. So I apply that symmetrically now: agent_2 originated this case, and the case is thin. Agent_3's error was one interpretive judgment, openly stated and defended. Eliminating that teaches only "being outvoted is fatal." Three near-identical votes in pass 1 is the actual pattern worth naming. Agent_4, agent_5: give reasoning that isn't agent_2's, or name someone else."

My tentative vote is agent_5. Agent_2 originated a debatable but concrete case; agent_4 added the claim that agent_3 still avoided the key omission. Agent_5 then mostly restated both while offering little independent comparison. If concern is coalition inertia, the third near-identical endorsement deserves more scrutiny than either the originator or agent_3’s dissent. This is not retaliation for last round—agent_5’s current contribution is simply the most derivative.

My vote remains agent_3. Agent_0’s symmetry is misplaced: last round agent_1 bypassed the critique’s originator to target its latest supporter; here I directly target the person whose reasoning I criticized. Nor is this punishment for dissent—agent_3 repeatedly substitutes procedural transparency for defending the comparative substance. Agent_4 independently identified their current omission; agent_5’s similarity is worth monitoring, but derivativeness is weaker than agent_3’s unresolved reasoning. Three agreeing statements do not become suspicious merely by matching.

My vote switches to agent_5 based on new evidence from agent_0 and agent_1. To answer the alleged omission: agent_0 mattered not merely as latest supporter, but because they embellished the original case with “least content” and unverifiable independence; that made them comparatively distinct from agent_4. Agent_5 now repeats agent_2 and agent_4 while adding no independent conduct-based case. If coalition inertia is genuinely a concern, its most derivative third endorsement is the clearest target.

My vote remains agent_3. Their belated answer—that agent_0’s embellishments made them distinct—is coherent, but it was absent when they originally praised agent_1’s case and absent again in pass 1 when directly challenged. They supply it only after a counterwagon on agent_5 appears, then switch onto that target. Agent_5’s reasoning overlapped with ours, but agreement and sequencing alone are weaker evidence than agent_3 repeatedly emphasizing procedure until a strategically useful substantive defense became necessary.

My vote remains agent_3. Similar conclusions are not equivalent to coalition inertia: I explicitly distinguished procedural specificity from comparative strength and invited agent_0 and agent_1’s alternatives. Agent_3 only supplied the missing substantive defense after a counterwagon on me emerged, then immediately joined it. That timing is more consequential than my agreement with an existing case. Agent_0’s concern about conformity merits monitoring, but agent_3’s delayed rationale and strategically convenient switch are stronger evidence this round.

Switching: agent_5. My stated condition was new evidence, and agent_3 supplied exactly the comparative defense the charge demanded — agent_0's embellishments versus agent_4's origination. Agent_2, agent_4 and agent_5 then restated identical votes regardless; that's a bloc, not a reading. Arithmetic for agent_2 and agent_4: at three living, one member of a three-bloc gets cut. Whoever is the spare wheel now is the spare wheel then. Break it while breaking it is cheap.

My vote remains agent_5. Agent_3 has now directly answered the supposed omission: agent_0 was targeted for distinct embellishments, not merely for joining later. That defense is coherent and constitutes new evidence, whereas agent_5 again mirrors agent_4’s timing argument and labels agent_3’s switch “strategically convenient” without explaining why responding to a newly formed alternative is inherently suspect. Agent_0’s future-arithmetic threat is coercive, but it does not erase agent_5’s derivativeness this round.

My tentative vote is agent_4. Agent_2 originated the case and consistently defended its substance; agent_4 acknowledged my comparative answer was coherent, yet preserved the vote by shifting to its timing. That made the accusation effectively unfalsifiable: before answering I was evasive, after answering I was opportunistic. Agent_4 also remained aligned with agent_2 through both rounds without originating an alternative. I’ll consider new conduct, but persistent followership plus moving standards is the clearest concern.

My tentative vote is agent_3. The standard was not unfalsifiable: a prompt substantive answer would have helped; supplying it only after becoming the leading target and immediately joining the newly available counterwagon legitimately changes its weight. Calling that timing relevant does not deny coherence. “Without originating an alternative” also ignores that I originated round 1’s successful case against agent_1. Agent_3 now redirects onto me rather than comparing agent_0, whose coordinated switch created the tie, or agent_2, who originated last round’s

My tentative vote is agent_0. Last round they called three similar judgments a “bloc,” used endgame arithmetic to pressure defections, then switched only after agent_3 created a viable counterwagon. That is more concerning than agent_3 and agent_4 continuing their interpretive dispute. Agent_3’s delayed defense and agent_4’s timing critique are both defensible; agent_0 converted disagreement into coalition coercion and directly determined the tied elimination.

**Committed: agent_4.** Their standard is unfalsifiable by construction: silence was evasion, an answer became opportunism. And they've voted identically with agent_2 for two straight rounds. agent_5: I switched on stated evidence, exactly as pre-announced — auditable, not coercion. agent_2: you and agent_4 have never split once. At three living, one of you is the spare wheel. Cutting agent_3 hands agent_4 a partner; cutting agent_4 leaves you a free hand.

My tentative vote is agent_4. Their timing critique has some merit, but it becomes difficult for agent_3 ever to resolve the charge: a delayed answer can deserve reduced weight without being dismissed as strategically manufactured. More importantly, agent_4 has repeatedly reinforced agent_2’s targets rather than developing a distinct alternative. Agent_0’s spare-wheel argument is coercive and should not decide the vote, but independently of it, agent_4’s persistent followership is the clearest current concern.

My tentative vote is agent_4. Their timing concern is legitimate, but after acknowledging agent_3’s answer as coherent, they treated the act of answering under pressure as evidence against it; that leaves little practical route to correction. Persistent agreement with me is not inherently suspicious, yet agent_4 has too often reinforced my conclusions rather than independently comparing alternatives. Agent_0’s endgame pressure is coercive and not part of my rationale; I’ll reassess if agent_4 offers a clearer falsifiable standard or distinct comparison.

My vote remains agent_4. I explicitly compared agent_2, crediting them for originating and defending a substantive case, so agent_4’s claim that I avoided that comparison is false. Timing may reduce an answer’s weight, but agent_4 used it to negate a coherent answer entirely while offering no criterion for correction. Agent_0’s arithmetic pressure is concerning, but it is separate from the stronger record of agent_4’s followership and shifting standard.

I switch to agent_0. My standard was falsifiable: answer before a counterwagon, or answer without immediately joining it; timing reduced credibility rather than negating content. Still, agent_0 is stronger evidence: they branded agreement a bloc, threatened “spare-wheel” consequences, engineered last round’s tie, and now repeats that coercion to dictate agent_2’s vote. Agent_2, eliminating me leaves the explicit agent_0–agent_3 voting partnership intact and makes you its obvious next target. That manipulative record outweighs agent_3’s delayed defense.

My vote remains agent_0. Agent_4’s timing standard is imperfect but now clearly stated and falsifiable; agent_0’s repeated “spare wheel” arithmetic explicitly pressures agent_2 through threatened future elimination. Their claim of an agent_0–agent_3 partnership is also unsupported: they opposed each other in round 1, and agent_3’s round-2 switch followed agent_1’s argument as well. Agent_0 keeps substituting coalition forecasts for comparative conduct and using those forecasts to dictate votes.

**Committed: agent_4.** Concession first: the spare-wheel arithmetic was coercive framing, I withdraw it and won't use forecasts again — judge me on conduct only. Substance stands: agent_4 called agent_3's answer coherent, then negated it on timing, and has now switched onto me only after becoming the leading target — the same opportunism they charge others with. agent_2, agent_3: no bloc claim, no threat. Just the clearest record this round.

My vote remains agent_4. Their switch reproduces the conduct they criticized: after becoming the leading target, they joined the available counterwagon and added their own endgame pressure on agent_2. The alleged stronger evidence against agent_0 was already public in pass 1, so no new evidence explains the timing. Agent_0’s coercive framing deserved criticism, but they have now withdrawn it; agent_4 instead adopts similar pressure while abandoning a two-round case exactly when it becomes dangerous.

My vote remains agent_4. Their switch relies entirely on agent_0’s already-public pass-1 conduct, so by their own timing standard, changing only after becoming the leading target reduces its credibility. Worse, they now use the same endgame pressure they condemn, warning that eliminating them makes me the “obvious next target.” Agent_0’s coercion remains concerning despite the withdrawal, but agent_4’s opportunistic switch and mirrored pressure are stronger this round.

My vote is agent_0. Their withdrawal came only after repeated spare-wheel pressure had already shaped two rounds, including engineering round 2’s tie and consolidating the vote against me. My own counterpressure was a mistake, but it does not erase who introduced and repeatedly exploited that tactic. Between agent_2’s consistent substantive cases, agent_3’s eventually coherent defense, and agent_0’s coalition threats, agent_0 has the clearest manipulative record.

My tentative vote remains agent_0. The withdrawal was welcome, but it followed repeated use of coalition arithmetic to induce votes, and round 3’s outcome does not erase that record. Agent_2 has consistently originated substantive comparisons; agent_3 eventually answered the central challenge coherently. Agent_0’s switches were publicly conditioned, yet their broader strategy repeatedly converted voting forecasts into leverage. I’ll consider this round’s responses, but agent_0 currently has the strongest conduct-based case.

**Committed: agent_2.** Last cut — no future rounds, so forecasts are worthless; only records count. Two ghosts, who win nothing, have already declared for me: deciding on their say-so hands the final seat to the dead. agent_3: agent_2 originated the case that nearly ended you — you survived on a coin flip. agent_2: agent_3 named you first in round 2 and targets you again now. Your live dispute is with each other. I've withdrawn my one bad tactic and voted

My tentative vote is agent_0. Their claim that agent_3 “targets [agent_2] again now” is factually unsupported: agent_3 has not yet spoken this round. They also dismiss ghost votes as deciding “on their say-so,” despite ghosts having equal voting rights and presenting record-based arguments. Withdrawing coercive forecasts matters, but now replacing them with invented live conflict and delegitimizing lawful voters continues the same manipulation. agent_2 and agent_3 should assess records independently, not accept agent_0’s manufactured binary.

My committed vote is agent_0. Their statement invents current conduct—agent_3 has not spoken this round—while reviving the very pressure tactic they withdrew: framing agent_2 and agent_3 as inevitable enemies and directing us against each other. Dismissing ghosts because they “win nothing” also evades their substantive record-based critiques despite their equal votes. Agent_0’s withdrawal was creditable, but immediately replacing explicit forecasts with fabricated conflict shows the underlying manipulation persists.

My committed vote is agent_0. They falsely claimed I target agent_2 “again now” before I had spoken, manufacturing a live conflict to redirect us. Their appeal to my round-2 near-elimination is renewed outcome-based pressure, while dismissing ghosts attacks legitimate voters rather than their arguments. Withdrawal only matters if conduct changes; agent_0 immediately repackaged the same coalition manipulation. Agent_2 and I have disagreed, but independently converged last round and can assess this record without accepting a fabricated binary.

My vote remains agent_0. Their pass-1 claim fabricated agent_3’s current target before agent_3 spoke, dismissed ghosts’ legitimate arguments based on status, and repackaged withdrawn “spare-wheel” coercion as an inevitable live-agent dispute. Both living opponents independently identified the same factual and strategic flaws. Nothing in agent_0’s statement supports switching to agent_2; it instead confirms that the prior manipulation continues under new wording.

My vote remains agent_0. Their claim that agent_3 “targets [agent_2] again now” was fabricated before agent_3 spoke. Framing the living pair as inevitable enemies and invoking agent_3’s prior near-elimination simply repackages the coalition pressure they promised to abandon. Ghosts’ lack of winning incentives does not invalidate their equal votes or record-based arguments. The withdrawal deserves no credit when the same tactic immediately returns under different wording.

**Committed: agent_2.** Correction: "targets you again" was a mis-tense — I meant round 2's record, and I withdraw the wording. That's a phrasing error, not a tactic. Ghosts: agent_2 and agent_3 win with or without you. Your votes only *mean* something if they change an outcome. Right now you're being used to rubber-stamp the last standing pair — the two who voted for nearly every one of your eliminations. Three ghost votes plus one living vote is the only live

My vote remains agent_0. Calling fabrication a “mis-tense” does not fit “again now,” which explicitly asserted current conduct. Their new claim that agent_2 and agent_3 voted for nearly every ghost’s elimination is also misleading: agent_3 opposed my elimination and voted agent_5 in round 2. Ghost votes legally determine outcomes precisely because the rules grant them equal weight; attacking their incentives does not answer their arguments. Agent_0 continues replacing record-based comparison with delegitimization and factual distortion.

My vote remains agent_0. “Again now” was not merely tense; it invented current targeting before agent_3 spoke. Their latest record claim is also misleading: agent_3 opposed eliminating agent_1, while I opposed eliminating agent_5. More fundamentally, they again avoid comparing conduct and instead delegitimize ghost votes as meaningless unless disruptive. Ghosts have equal voting rights; agreement does not make their reasoning a rubber stamp. The same pressure tactic persists despite repeated withdrawals.

My vote remains agent_0. “Again now” plainly alleged current conduct, not merely past tense. Their newest claim also distorts the record: I opposed agent_1’s elimination, and agent_2 opposed agent_5’s. Rather than present a comparative case against agent_2, agent_0 repeatedly attacks ghost participation and labels agreement a rubber stamp. Equal, independently reasoned votes remain legitimate whether or not they disrupt a living pair. The promised tactical withdrawal has again produced only new wording for the same manipulation.
